title: Liege: the Regina Dance Hall and friends Koks and Pagneule
summary: At the Regina Dance Hall in Liege he befriended the trumpeter Alfonse Koks and pianist Marcel Pagneule, both of whom later came to Paris or replaced him in Vienna.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: And I must say that we had a really wonderful time. We went to Liege.

The Regina Dance Hall. And there I made some wonderful friends. I met a wonderful trumpet player who was -- he was doing his military service in one of the bands. Pardon me. His name was Alfonse Koks. He was of Dutch origin. Not German, Dutch, origin. His name was Koks.

And he played violin-cello, as well. He was in the second orchestra, but he only played violin-cello in the orchestra. When we were over for the night after the show, he came over and spoke to me, he said, "Well, I play trumpet as well." He said, "I'm first brass at the conservatory."
We became friends like that, up to his death, just about three years ago, because he came to Paris after.
And I had a pianist who was in an orchestra, not a straight orchestra, they played waltzes, and tangoes and schottisches and things like that, you know.
And the pianist who was in the
orchestra, also came to Paris. His name is on the tip of my tongue. Pagneule.
Pagneule. He died also. He died about fifteen years ago. Marcel Pagneule.
And we all became friends, and with the other members of both orchestras, we became friends, and it's just one of those things.
Koks, seeing Koks the second time after I left Liege, he came to Vienna, to replace me in the band. He came in the band that replaced me in Vienna.
I'll talk about Vienna and Germany tomorrow, when we have more time.
